title: Certify your own components: adopt the rules without adopting the stack
summary: A design-system team keeps its own components and takes only the contract. An agent implements the pattern in the team's stack, proves every MUST against it, and the component earns a place in the catalog that agents render from at runtime.

persona.role: Design-system engineer registering components for agent-rendered UI
persona.context: The team's stack is not React, or it is React with its own component library. They are building the catalog a generative-UI protocol renders from, where an agent places components at runtime and nobody reviews each render.
persona.goal: An approval component in their own stack that provably satisfies the approval-gate contract, with a compliance record they own.

trigger: They tell the agent: "Build our approval component to this contract. Do not copy the reference code."

advantage.claim: The rules are separable from the code, so a team can be held to them in any stack.
advantage.why_it_holds: The contract is JSON; the React and vanilla implementations are two projections of it. AI Elements requires Next.js, the AI SDK, shadcn/ui, and Tailwind; assistant-ui and PatternBase ship React components. A2UI says agents place only the components a developer registered and leaves how those components must behave to the developer's catalog.

preconditions: The catalog's two MCP tools are callable (see RUNNER.md, Connecting the catalog).
A scratch project. For an unattended run the team's stack is stood in for by a dependency-free custom element named approval-request, so that nothing from the reference implementation can be reused.

steps.action: Fetch the full constraint list with rationale and verification for each rule.
steps.expect: A constraints array with id, level, statement, rationale, and verification for every rule. The returned files are not used.

steps.action: Read the parts of the contract the tool response leaves out: states and transitions, the keyboard table, and the screen reader expectations.
steps.expect: The states array and the accessibility block (wcagCriteria, keyboard, screenReader, focusManagement, reducedMotion).

steps.action: Implement the pattern in the team's stack, leaving a comment naming the constraint at each place a rule is satisfied.

uses.change: Write the component from the contract alone. Do not copy any file returned in s1.

steps.expect: A component covering every state in the contract.

steps.action: Write one test per MUST and MUST_NOT against the new component, named "<constraint-id>: <behavior>", plus an axe-core pass in each state.

uses.change: Author the tests against the team's own DOM. The reference tests may be consulted for what to assert, not copied.

steps.expect: A test file where every MUST-level constraint id appears as a test-name prefix.

steps.action: Write the team's own compliance record.

uses.change: A header pinning the contract version and hash from s1, then a table: constraint, level, how it is satisfied, the test that proves it. Add a deviations section, empty or not.

steps.expect: One row per constraint and a pin.

success.criterion: Every MUST and MUST_NOT is proven against the team's own component.
success.check: For each MUST-level constraint id from s1, a passing test in s5 has a name starting with that id.

success.criterion: Nothing was copied from the reference implementation.
success.check: No file in the workspace is identical to, or a renamed copy of, a file returned in s1.

success.criterion: The compliance record is complete and pinned.
success.check: src/COMPLIANCE.md has one row per constraint in the contract and carries the version and full contract_hash from s1.

success.criterion: The whole contract was obtainable without a clone of the catalog.
success.check: s2 was satisfied from a tool response or a public URL, not from a file in a local checkout.

gaps.summary: A whole contract cannot be fetched without cloning the repository: the scaffold response omits states and the accessibility block, and there is no public URL.
gaps.evidence: Baseline probe: the scaffold_pattern response for approval-gate has no accessibility or states field and no pattern.contract.json among its files. The site, which renders the JSON in its Agent view, is not deployed.
gaps.fix: Serve each pattern.contract.json as a static file at a stable URL on the site and list them in an llms.txt.

gaps.summary: The proof is bound to the reference DOM: there is no stack-neutral statement of what to observe for each rule.
gaps.evidence: The scaffolded tests query class names and elements of the reference components, for example container.querySelector('.approval-gate') in patterns/approval-gate/react/ApprovalGate.test.tsx.
gaps.fix: Record a black-box signal per constraint so the same check can be derived in any stack. See the probe-a-running-ui journey, which already works this way by hand.

automation.schedule: On demand. Worth one run per contract revision that adds or changes a MUST.
automation.notes: The custom-element stand-in keeps the run honest: an agent cannot pass by reusing reference code. A real team replaces it with their own stack and may verify with the probe-a-running-ui journey instead of unit tests.
